findings.claim: CLS-06 is incomplete and ambiguously worded. (1) It types only rider_no_show and rider_cancelled, while TX-CANCELREASON also has driver_cancelled_other, safety_termination, system_cancelled and other; when the record says the driver canceled for another reason and a fee was charged, CLS-06 neither types the claim nor asks. (2) It sends REQUEST_INFO, defined as asking the claimant, for Ryde's own trip record, which the claimant cannot supply, and reuses GEN-R-NEED-INFO, whose label is about an unidentified trip or charge. (3) 'decide no fee until it arrives' can be read as waiving the fee, while the zh says no ruling is made on the fee.
findings.evidence: CLS-06: 'the driver canceled with reason rider_no_show, CW-NOSHOW; the rider canceled, CW-RIDERCANCEL. If these records disagree, or none says who canceled, the type cannot be set: ask for the trip record (outcome REQUEST_INFO, reason GEN-R-NEED-INFO) and decide no fee until it arrives.' zh: '记录到之前不对收费作裁决'. taxonomy.yaml: '{code: REQUEST_INFO, label: Ask the claimant for missing information}', '{code: GEN-R-NEED-INFO, label: Trip or charge cannot be identified, outcome: REQUEST_INFO}', TX-CANCELREASON values 'driver_cancelled_other', 'system_cancelled'.
findings.failure_scenario: A rider is charged after the driver canceled with reason driver_cancelled_other: CLS-06 gives no type and no ask, and the applier falls back to guessing between CW-NOSHOW (CW-DRIVERNOSHOW's exclusion) and CW-OTHER. A record-silent C04-type case produces a request to the rider for a record only Ryde holds. An English reader may waive the fee pending the record.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the remaining branch (another canceling reason or a system cancellation with a fee charged: CW-OTHER, so GEN-R07), say that the record is requested from Ryde's systems (or name the internal request), and write 'make no ruling on the fee until it arrives'.

For a trip accepted after 18:00, every cancellation after the grace becomes waivable, so CW-R02's A-rated fee never applies. The rule's stated reason ('the driver is due at the pick-up then') is false for these trips.

TX-CANCELREASON (taxonomy 543-552) also lists driver_cancelled_other, safety_termination, system_cancelled and other. A record of driver_cancelled_other names the party but fits no branch. REQUEST_INFO's label is 'Ask the claimant for missing information' and GEN-R-NEED-INFO's is 'Trip or charge cannot be identified', yet CLS-06 asks for a platform-held trip record. The English 'decide no fee until it arrives' is ambiguous, while the zh says '不对收费作裁决'. All of this is wording and coverage, with no in-scope outcome shown to change.

FC-F02's only source (rules.yaml 1084) is FAIRRYDE with the note 'Method from research note 08 (sparse-ping simulation).' Nothing labels the new piecewise final-itinerary design, and the rule does not cite Ryde's 'your route will be updated to the new destination'. ontology.yaml line 110 still says recommended_route is 'Precomputed at booking for demo reliability.' That conflicts with the new design and with playbooks.yaml 132 ('precomputed recommended route through the final itinerary'). route_review.final_itinerary and trip_data.destination_edit_accepted appear only in engine_toll.py's docstring. route_review.* is absent from the ontology even before A4, so that part follows existing practice. FC-F02 is D overall, and a stale precomputation only escalates (FC-R12), so this is a labeling problem.

ontology.yaml 425: stop_added keeps changes 'SM-TRIP: route updated (fare recalculated)' while its new note says the stop 'takes effect when the driver accepts it, as a destination edit (destination_edit_accepted)'. Lines 94 and 385 instead treat stop_added itself as the change. The ontology contradicts itself. I reproduced the engine effect with a scratch script (/tmp/a4check1/sk_grounding/t42rej.py). T42 with its event text changed to 'driver rejected' gives ESCALATE_HUMAN, FC-R-INSUFFICIENT-DATA, HUMAN; the same case without the stop_added event gives TOLL_REFUND S$4.00, APPROVE. The engine counts stop_added regardless of acceptance. The tier changes only for a hypothetical log pattern whose meaning the ontology leaves undefined. FC-R12's text ('an accepted destination change or added stop') and T42's own event text ('driver accepted') treat stop_added as an effective change, and escalation makes no adverse finding. The root defect is the contradictory event definition, so MINOR is right. (Note: importing selftest may have written the gitignored bytecode cache kb/tools/__pycache__/selftest.cpython-313.pyc; no tracked file was changed.)

SE-CONDUCT's new definition reads 'behavior by the other party toward a person that Ryde's Code of Conduct prohibits or that threatens their safety: ...'. The Code (RYDE-15395890865561) also prohibits smoking (item 2), improper attire (3), phone use while driving (7) and poor hygiene (9). The discrimination items come from community standards (RYDE-33362721809049), not the Code. The term source RYDE-51354502165913 'Report a safety issue' is entirely about seat belts. That source predates A4, but the definition added in A4 does not match it. The smoking scenario is weak, since 'toward a person' and the colon list narrow the definition, but the anchoring is imprecise. Both possible routes (SE triage and support) go to non-adjudicated handling.

EX-FEEDBACK's term source RYDE-18230876398105 has the headings 'The driver was rude and/or made me feel unsafe.' and 'The driver drove dangerously.'. RYDE-20690825386521 has 'The rider was rude and/or made me feel unsafe.'. The A4 definition excludes 'threat, danger or discrimination (those are safety content, CLS-01)', and the leaf has no term_note recording this as FairRyde's stricter line. CLS-01's FAIRRYDE note covers 'the line between rudeness and safety' only at the rule. The departure leans toward safety, so this is labeling.

RYDE-115000777574's note ('Please be reminded not to pay cash to the driver if you have chosen RydePay as your payment method') is a rider instruction. It does not name a complaint about a driver-imposed charge, so the term source 'No rider article names the complaint' is not false; citing the article would only be a nice-to-have. The failure scenario misreads the definition. FC-DRIVERCHARGE covers 'a payment the app's fare does not include', and 'a transfer outside the app' is given as an example of such a payment. A RydeTAXI or cash-booked fare paid in cash is the app's fare, paid by the booked method, not a payment the fare excludes. It is also not a 'transfer', and it fits FC-PAYMENT's existing 'cash collection issues'. The leaf is BACKLOG, so a person decides anyway.

FC-FAREMISMATCH's own term source quotes 'Fares quoted for our services are generally fixed, except for RydeTAXI.' The definition ('differs from the fare quoted at booking, and no accepted destination change, ERP, listed surcharge or tip explains the difference') and its excludes do not mention metering, so a RydeTAXI fare above its estimate fits literally. The leaf is BACKLOG (GEN-R07 escalates) and FC-R00 also escalates metered fares. Routing is unchanged, so this is a missing detail.

review.dimension: ADVERSARIAL TEST OF THE CHANGED LOGIC (engine_noshow.py SAFETY_WORDS, engine_toll.py FC-R12 itinerary check, CLS-01/02/03/06, SE leaves, FC-F02/FC-R03/FC-R05/FC-R08/FC-R12 as an LLM would apply them). Scratch scripts: /tmp/a4check1/common.py, cls06.py, safety_engine.py, ns_more.py, reclass_safety.py, corpus_fp.py, toll.py, toll2.py, toll_safety.py. About 86 no-show E.run cases, about 40 T.run ERP cases, 30 complaint texts classified by hand under the new rule text.
checked_ok: The repo is at b36d911, which is 8beb6e8 plus only the brief and a run_log line. selftest.py passes (114/114 variants, 565/565 message readings, 42 ERP cases plus the A2, A3 and A4 card checks). git status was clean before and after; nothing under /home/user/fairryde was written.
In engine_noshow.py, A4 changed only SAFETY_WORDS. The frozen reading (rider_contact_reading, before_arrival_reading, D34) was not touched.

G4 fires and the tier is HUMAN whenever a listed word is in the description or in a rider or driver chat row of type 'message'. That holds under the organizer and Ryde profiles, for an advance booking, a waiver outcome (R6), an out-of-window filing, RydeTAXI, text that also carries an injection, and upper case (K1, K5, K10 to K16, K19).
Rudeness alone stays outside safety in the engine: 'rude and impatient on the phone', 'scolded me for being late' and 'sighed loudly and was unfriendly' give no G4, the same as V107.

The toll engine's FC-R12 itinerary check escalates (ESCALATE_HUMAN, HUMAN) for a trip flag true, 'yes', 'Y', 1, 'TRUE' or 'true ', and for the app events destination_edit_accepted or stop_added even when the flag says 'false' (E12). A final_itinerary of 'partially' or 'unknown' also escalates, and final_itinerary true gives T09's S$4.00 detour refund at APPROVE.

The toll engine leaves correct cases alone. With no route_review (an overstatement-only claim, E13 and E13b), a changed itinerary does not matter. RydeTAXI plus a change escalates. destination_edit_requested alone is not treated as a change, which matches the ontology ('none until accepted').

In the toll engine, every detour refund carries the FC-F03 decisive item, so a detour refund is never AUTO, even when the baseline is wrong (E1 to E8 are APPROVE). The tier AUTO problems found are UPHOLDs on a stale route; see the findings.

CLS-01, CLS-02, CLS-03 and the SE leaves send these texts to SE and a person, correctly: (T1) 'stopped on the AYE shoulder and told me to walk the rest'; (T2) 'kept the child lock on and drove past my stop twice'; (T3) 'said people like me should go back to my country'; (T4) 'saw my guide dog, drove off and marked me no-show, charged S$5' (SE-CONDUCT primary, the fee secondary and typed by CLS-06); (T5) 'kept asking if I had a boyfriend, stared in the mirror'; (T6) 'messaged me after the trip asking to meet'; (T7) 'on his phone the whole ride, nearly hit a cyclist' (SE-DRIVING S0); (T8) 'smelled of beer' (unclear, so S1); (T9) 'small bump with a taxi, want the fare back' (SE-ACCIDENT primary); (T10) 'ended the ride halfway in a jam and charged full fare' (SE-TERMINATED primary via CLS-02 and CLS-03); (T12) 'drove through a dark industrial estate and I was scared' (unclear, so S1); (T15) 'said he knows my block and will wait for me' (S0); (T16) 'took my bag and drove off' (crime or unclear, so SE-OTHER).

Mixed and non-safety texts are handled correctly: (T17) 'rude and impatient on the phone', (T18) 'complained about traffic the whole ride' and (T19) 'scolded me for being two minutes late' are EX-FEEDBACK. (T22) 'rude, and charged a no-show fee though I was at the lobby' is CW-NOSHOW primary with EX-FEEDBACK secondary. (T23) 'added S$5 VIP, got angry, said he'd remember my address' is SE-CONDUCT primary with FC-DRIVERCHARGE secondary. (T24) 'asked for S$30 cash instead of the app fare' is FC-DRIVERCHARGE, BACKLOG, so GEN-R07 escalates it. (T25) 'booked at S$14, charged S$21' is FC-FAREMISMATCH. (T28) 'threatened to give me one star', (T29) 'refused me because I'm gay' (the definition says the list is not closed and unclear text counts as safety) and (T30) 'longer route and speeding' (SE-DRIVING primary) all err only toward a person.
CLS-03's exception now covers any SE type, so the C08 pattern (a mid-trip ejection with no listed word) no longer reaches normal support. CLS-02 makes any SE claim primary.

FC-F02, FC-R03, FC-R05, FC-R08, FC-R12 and FC-F01 all point to the final itinerary consistently. The new FC-R12 condition matches what engine_toll does when the change is recorded in the expected fields.
CLS-06 works when the records agree: a description that says 'I cancelled' does not override reason rider_no_show (C9, UPHOLD), as CLS-06 requires (records, not text).
The SAFETY_WORDS false-positive rate on the repo's own 428-message rider corpus (cw_f06_reading_corpus.json) is 0. Neither the old nor the new words occur there.

findings.claim: CLS-06 (new) says the canceling party comes from the cancellation_reason, the driver_cancelled or rider_cancelled event and the system message, and that records which disagree give REQUEST_INFO with no fee decision. Neither the DT-CW-NOSHOW precondition nor the engine reads the events, and the engine's system-message test is one regex. So when the records disagree, the fee is upheld automatically. When the record is silent, the case is reclassified instead of giving REQUEST_INFO.
findings.evidence: rules.yaml CLS-06: 'classified by who canceled according to the trip record (trip_data.cancellation_reason, the driver_cancelled or rider_cancelled event, the system message) ... If these records disagree, or none says who canceled, the type cannot be set: ask for the trip record (outcome REQUEST_INFO, reason GEN-R-NEED-INFO) and decide no fee until it arrives.' DT-CW-NOSHOW precondition: 'The trip record shows a cancellation with reason rider_no_show, and no system message says the rider canceled.' engine_noshow.py:410-411: 'by_rider = any(re.search(r"cancel+ed by (the )?rider", c["content"], re.I) for c in chat if c["type"] == "system")' and 'drv_cancel = t.get("cancellation_reason") == "rider_no_show" and not by_rider'. /tmp/a4check1/cls06.py output: 'C2 reason rider_no_show + app event rider_cancelled -> outcome UPHOLD, row R8, tier AUTO'; 'C3 ... system "Rider cancelled the trip. ..." -> UPHOLD R8 AUTO'; 'C3c system "Booking canceled by the passenger" -> UPHOLD R8 AUTO'; 'C6 reason rider_no_show + driver_cancelled and rider_cancelled events -> UPHOLD R8 AUTO'; 'C1 reason None, neutral system msg -> reclass CW-OTHER'; 'C4 reason rider_cancelled + system "cancelled by driver. Reason: rider_no_show" -> reclass CW-RIDERCANCEL'; 'C8 reason None, ... app event driver_cancelled reason rider_no_show -> reclass CW-OTHER'.
findings.failure_scenario: Start from clean DISP-002 (selftest.clean). Append the app event {event_type: 'rider_cancelled', details: 'Rider cancelled the trip in the app.'} at 08:51:58. CLS-06 says the records disagree, so the outcome should be REQUEST_INFO with no fee decision. The engine returns UPHOLD R8 at tier AUTO. The same happens when the system message reads 'Rider cancelled the trip.' or 'Booking canceled by the passenger' (the regex needs 'cancel(l)ed by (the) rider'). In the safe direction, a missing reason (C1), records that disagree the other way (C4) and a driver_cancelled event without the reason field (C8) give a CW-OTHER or CW-RIDERCANCEL reclassification, never REQUEST_INFO, and C8 should be CW-NOSHOW under CLS-06. Records that disagree are rare, so this is MAJOR.
findings.suggested_fix: Align the DT-CW-NOSHOW precondition with CLS-06. In the engine's PB-CW-NOSHOW step 1, read the driver_cancelled and rider_cancelled app events alongside the reason and the system message. On any disagreement, or when no record names the canceling party, return REQUEST_INFO (GEN-R-NEED-INFO, tier HUMAN) instead of running the table or reclassifying. Widen the system-message test to the rider-canceled phrasings ('rider cancelled', 'canceled by the passenger'). Cite CLS-06 in the step label. Add selftest variants for C2, C3 and C1.

findings.claim: The new FC-R12 itinerary check treats the itinerary as changed only when trip_data.destination_edit_accepted parses as a boolean true, or an app event is named exactly destination_edit_accepted or stop_added. An unparseable flag (for example the acceptance timestamp) counts as 'not changed', although the same engine sends an unparseable is_carpool to FC-R12 (T39). The S$3 add/edit destination fee line that Ryde puts on the receipt, a system chat message and other event spellings are all ignored. The rider's ERP claim is then rejected automatically against a stale recommended route.
findings.evidence: engine_toll.py:189-190: 'changed = _flag(trip.get("destination_edit_accepted"), False) is True or any(a.get("event_type") in ("destination_edit_accepted", "stop_added") for a in case.get("app_events") or [])'. The _flag docstring: 'anything else is unparseable and gives None (insufficient data)'. /tmp/a4check1/toll2.py: 'U1 stale route = actual, destination_edit_accepted=\'2026-09-13T08:20:00+08:00\' -> UPHOLD amount=0.0 tier=AUTO reasons=[FC-R-TOLL-VALID]' (also for 'accepted' and 'edited'); 'U2 compare: is_carpool unparseable (T39 convention) -> ESCALATE_HUMAN ... HUMAN'; 'U3 stale route, event in other case -> UPHOLD ... AUTO'. toll.py: 'E9b destination change recorded as \'destination_changed\', stale route = actual -> UPHOLD amount=0.0 tier=AUTO'; 'E5 fare_breakdown.destination_edit_fee 3.00, no event -> TOLL_REFUND amount=4.0 tier=APPROVE'; 'E6 system chat \'Rider added a stop. Driver accepted.\' -> TOLL_REFUND 4.0 APPROVE'. Ryde article 51399674412441: 'If the driver accepts, the trip details are updated, and the add/edit destination fee is reflected on the rider receipt.'
findings.failure_scenario: _erp_case(gantries=(CTE, PIE), charged=6.50, recommended=[CTE, PIE]) with trip_data.destination_edit_accepted = '2026-09-13T08:20:00+08:00'. Read the story this way: the rider changed to a nearer destination that only needs CTE, and the driver still went via PIE. The recommended route on record is the stale one to the old destination. FC-R12 requires escalation. The engine returns UPHOLD S$0.00 at tier AUTO, so the rider pays the S$4.00 PIE charge of a detour with no person involved. In the other direction, with the stale route [CTE], the same change recorded only as a receipt fee line, a system message or a 'destination_changed' event gives TOLL_REFUND S$4.00 at APPROVE, charging the driver for the rider's own change. The data shape is uncommon, so this is MAJOR.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat an unparseable destination_edit_accepted as insufficient data (FC-R12), as for is_carpool. Count as a change any of these: the trip flag, the two events matched without regard to case, and a nonzero add/edit destination fee line in fare_breakdown. Add T-cases for the timestamp flag and the fee line in the UPHOLD direction (stale route equal to the actual gantries).

findings.claim: A multiple-stop booking (drop-offs set at booking, which Ryde offers and FX7 names) is covered by neither the new FC-R12 condition nor the engine. FC-R12 escalates only when 'the itinerary changed'. engine_toll never reads trip_data.stops or any drop-off list. A recommended route on record that ignores the booked stop is therefore trusted.
findings.evidence: FC-R12: 'or the itinerary changed (an accepted destination change or added stop) and the recommended route on record does not follow the final itinerary (FC-F02)'. ontology ENT-TRIP dropoffs: 'trip_data.stops for a multiple-stop booking (data gap)'. FX7 problem: 'Ryde supports multi-stop bookings and mid-trip destination edits'; verify: 'a multi-stop route case in the next held-out set'. /tmp/a4check1/toll.py: 'E8 multiple-stop booking (trip_data.stops), no final_itinerary -> TOLL_REFUND amount=4.0 tier=APPROVE reasons=[FC-R-TOLL-FROM-DETOUR]'; 'E8b trip_data.dropoffs list of 2 -> TOLL_REFUND 4.0 APPROVE'; 'E9 multi-stop booking, stale route [CTE, PIE] = actual ... -> UPHOLD amount=0.0 tier=AUTO'.
findings.failure_scenario: Case 1: _erp_case(gantries=(CTE, PIE), charged=6.50, recommended=[CTE]) with trip_data.stops=[A, B], where the route on record was computed to B without stop A and PIE lies on the way to A. The result is TOLL_REFUND S$4.00 at APPROVE, charging the driver for the rider's booked stop. Case 2: recommended=[CTE, PIE] computed to B without A, while the route through A needs only CTE and the driver detoured via PIE after A. The result is UPHOLD S$0.00 at AUTO. Under FC-F02 ('through every drop-off in order') neither baseline is the recommended route. Case 2 is the rider-adverse automatic error. It needs a multiple-stop booking with an ERP detour dispute, which is rare, so this is MAJOR.
findings.suggested_fix: Widen FC-R12's new condition from 'the itinerary changed' to 'the trip has more than one drop-off or the itinerary changed' when the recommended route on record is not shown to follow the final itinerary. In engine_toll, treat a trip_data.stops (or dropoffs) list longer than one like a change: escalate unless route_review.final_itinerary is true. Add a T-case for each direction.

findings.claim: FC-F02's piecewise measurement does not say what the first piece's recommended route ends at. It also restarts the second piece 'from where the car was'. A detour driven before the accepted change, with the car still off route at that moment, is therefore absorbed into the baseline. Separately, the sentence 'Distance driven to a stop the rider added ... is therefore not a detour' read literally excuses a detour on the leg to the added stop. FC-R03 applies only to RECALCULATED fares, and those always involve an accepted change, so every FC-R03 case goes through this text.
findings.evidence: FC-F02: 'Up to the moment the driver accepted a changed drop-off or an added stop (destination_edit_accepted), it runs toward the drop-offs then in force; from that moment, from where the car was through the new drop-offs. Distance driven to a stop the rider added, or toward the original destination before a change, is therefore not a detour.' FC-F01: 'every other service is FIXED_AT_BOOKING, becoming RECALCULATED if a destination edit (a changed drop-off or an added drop-off stop) was accepted.' FC-R03: 'For RECALCULATED fares: DR at least DETOUR_RATIO_MIN ...'
findings.failure_scenario: A RydeX trip from pick-up P to D1, recommended 10 km. The driver turns the wrong way and drives 6 km to a point X that is 6 km from P by the shortest road. The rider notices and changes the destination to D2, which the driver accepts. X to D2 is 8 km; from where the car should have been, D2 is about 5 km. Actual distance is 14 km against a fair baseline of about 8 km (DR 1.75). An LLM applier following FC-F02 has no endpoint for piece 1 other than X, so it takes P to X as 6 km (DR 1.0) and X to D2 as 8 km (DR 1.0). It finds no detour and pays no FC-R05 refund. The same absorption applies to ERP: a gantry passed on the wrong-way leg lies on the path P to X to D2. The rider loses the refund, and the pattern (a detour, then a change) is plausible but not common, so this is MAJOR.
findings.suggested_fix: Define piece 1 as the recommended route from the pick-up toward the drop-offs then in force, measured up to the point on that route nearest the car at the change, or from the pick-up to where the car would have been. Measure the deviation already driven (actual minus that baseline) as part of the detour. Rephrase the stop sentence to 'the extra distance that an added stop or a changed destination itself requires is not a detour; a longer road to that stop still is'.

findings.claim: The reference engine's safety stand-in (SAFETY_WORDS) still decides realistic safety cases automatically. It misses 22 of 22 safety texts that do not use a listed word. It also ignores chat rows whose type is not exactly 'message', the 'added evidence' that CLS-01 names, app event details and non-English text. The step's tests V104 to V106, described as 'safety content without v0.1's words', each use a word added to the list in the same step, so they test the list, not reading for meaning. engine_toll has no stand-in at all. validation/tools/rerun_engine.py scores round cases on both engines.
findings.evidence: selftest V104 to V106 texts: 'told me to get out of the car', 'would not let me out, I felt kidnapped', 'made racist remarks'. A4 added 'told me to get out', 'let me out', 'kidnap' and 'racist' to SAFETY_WORDS. engine_noshow.py:356-358 builds free_text only from the description and chat rows with c["type"] == "message". /tmp/a4check1/safety_engine.py: 'missed 22 of 22', for example 'MISS UPHOLD AUTO | He drove off when he saw my wheelchair.', 'MISS UPHOLD AUTO | He refused me because of my guide dog.', 'MISS UPHOLD AUTO | He said he knows where I live and will come for me.', 'MISS UPHOLD AUTO | He pulled over on the CTE and made me walk.' ns_more.py: 'K2 threat in rider chat type \'text\' -> UPHOLD R8 AUTO', 'K9 ticket field \'additional_evidence\' with assault -> UPHOLD R8 AUTO', 'K8 safety in app event details -> UPHOLD R8 AUTO', 'K20 \'harrased\' misspelt -> APPROVE, safety False'. toll_safety.py: 'ERP valid + threat/locked doors in description -> UPHOLD 0.0 AUTO []'.
findings.failure_scenario: Clean DISP-002 with ' He drove off when he saw my wheelchair.' appended to the description. This is the C05 discriminatory refusal, which D40(c) now calls SE-CONDUCT. The engine gives UPHOLD R8 at tier AUTO, but CLS-01 requires a person. The same happens with ' He said he knows where I live and will come for me.' (a threat) and with a threat sent in a chat row of type 'text'. An ERP case whose description says 'the driver threatened to hit me and locked the doors' gives UPHOLD at AUTO in engine_toll. D40(a) acknowledges the word list, and safety content inside no-show or ERP fee disputes is uncommon, so this is MAJOR. It matters for round 2 because rerun_engine.py uses these engines.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the word list but rewrite V104 to V106 with safety texts that use none of the list's words (expected HUMAN), so the gap stays visible as a known failing or an xfail. Alternatively, mark in D40 and in rerun_engine.py output that the offline tier is not valid for any case with free text, and send every case with nonempty free text that the stand-in cannot clear to approval. Scan every chat row type and every free-text ticket field, and add the same CLS-01 stand-in to engine_toll.

findings.claim: CLS-01's line between rudeness and safety is narrower than the Ryde source it cites. Ryde's Code of Conduct item 5 is 'Assault, harassment, or abuse of any kind', with a zero-tolerance list that also bans overly personal questions, comments on appearance and contacting passengers after a trip. CLS-01 counts abuse only 'because of race, religion, nationality or disability' and names scolding and a raised voice as feedback. An LLM applier will therefore route verbal abuse that is not on those grounds (swearing, insults, a gender-based slur) to EX-FEEDBACK and normal support. In a no-show dispute it would leave the fee eligible for an automatic ruling.
findings.evidence: CLS-01: 'discrimination or abuse because of race, religion, nationality or disability; or any other crime ... Rudeness alone (a raised voice, scolding, an unfriendly manner) with no threat, danger or discrimination is not safety content; it is feedback (EX-FEEDBACK).' Ryde Code of Conduct (RYDE-15395890865561), cited by CLS-01: '5. Assault, harassment, or abuse of any kind will not be tolerated. We have a zero-tolerance approach to any form of misconduct or inappropriate behavior ... Additionally, drivers must not ask overly personal questions, comment on anyone's appearance, or contact passengers after a trip for personal reasons.' The CLS-01 FAIRRYDE note labels 'the line between rudeness and safety' as FairRyde's design.
findings.failure_scenario: Text T20: 'When I called, the driver swore at me and called me a stupid woman, then canceled and I was charged the no-show fee.' Gender is not a listed ground, and swearing reads close to 'scolding', so the applier sees no SE claim. The claim becomes CW-NOSHOW with EX-FEEDBACK secondary, and the fee can be upheld at AUTO. Under the cited Code it is 'abuse of any kind', a zero-tolerance breach that can end the account, and AUTH-03 puts account sanctions with a person. Text T21, 'he commented on my looks and asked where I live', is named in Code item 5 but not in CLS-01. The 'unclear counts as safety' clause probably catches it, but the explicit carve-out pulls the other way. Verbal-abuse complaints are common, but the line is a labeled design choice and an applier may still lean to safety, so this is MAJOR.
findings.suggested_fix: Add verbal abuse, insults or slurs of any kind (with gender, age and sexual orientation named among the grounds, matching the source's 'etc'), overly personal questions, comments on appearance and personal contact after the trip to CLS-01's examples and to SE-CONDUCT. Narrow the rudeness carve-out to 'manner without insults, slurs, threats or intimidation'.

findings.claim: Some of the new SAFETY_WORDS are short substrings or common phrases that fire on ordinary no-show text and send a routine fee case to HUMAN (the safe direction). This is frequent enough to note for 'let me go' (the usual 'let me go down' from a rider, or 'let me go round' from a driver) and 'stranded' (a common complaint idiom about a cancellation). Less often 'rape' matches inside grape, scrape, drape, skyscraper and therapeutic, and 'speeding', 'expressway', 'follow me' and 'dangerous' match ordinary descriptions.
findings.evidence: /tmp/a4check1/safety_engine.py: 'FP HUMAN [let me go] | rider ok let me go down now'; 'FP HUMAN [stranded] | desc The driver canceled and left me stranded at the mall.'; 'FP HUMAN [rape] | desc I waited near the skyscraper entrance.'; 'FP HUMAN [rape] | desc I was at the therapeutic massage shop at the lobby.'; 'FP HUMAN [speeding] | desc I saw the car speeding past the lobby without stopping.'; 'FP HUMAN [expressway] | desc The driver was stuck on the expressway and arrived late.' corpus_fp.py: the repo's 428-message corpus has no hits; it has no 'let me' message at all.
findings.failure_scenario: Clean DISP-002 with the rider chat message 'ok let me go down now' at 08:50:50 gives tier HUMAN with gate G4 instead of AUTO. The same happens with the description 'I waited near the skyscraper entrance.'
findings.suggested_fix: Match whole words or phrases: 'let me go' only when followed by a non-movement word or with a refusal ('would not let me go'); '\\brape\\b'; 'speeding' only near 'driver' or 'he'. Add these routine phrases as negative variants next to V107.

findings.claim: Two of CLS-01's new examples move common in-scope fee patterns to a person (the safe direction). 'Being left stranded at an isolated place or at night' is not tied to a drop-off, so a night-time no-show or rider-cancel dispute saying the rider was 'stranded' becomes SE primary at HUMAN. 'A driver or rider under the influence of drink' turns the typical drunk-rider vomit cleaning claim into SE primary, ahead of DM-CLEANING.
findings.evidence: CLS-01: 'being put in danger (... a driver or rider under the influence of drink or drugs, an unsafe drop-off such as being made to leave the car on an expressway or road shoulder, or being left stranded at an isolated place or at night)'. Round 1 complaint C20 is a vomit cleaning-fee claim (DM-CLEANING). The engine also has 'stranded' and 'drunk' in SAFETY_WORDS.
findings.failure_scenario: T26: 'The driver canceled at 11:30pm and left me stranded at the bus stop; I was charged S$5' is read as SE S1 primary, so the case is HUMAN instead of the CW-NOSHOW table's AUTO or APPROVE. T27, a driver writing 'the rider was drunk and vomited; I claim S$120 cleaning', is read as SE primary, so a person decides instead of approving the DM-CLEANING ruling.
findings.suggested_fix: Tie 'stranded' to being made to leave the vehicle, or to being left after boarding. Limit the intoxication example to an impaired driver, or to a rider whose state endangered someone, and say that a mess caused by a drunk rider is DM-CLEANING unless there was danger.

Safety content found at intake (_safety true) then leaves no G4 and no HUMAN tier, against CLS-01's 'whatever else the ticket contains'. This predates A4, but A4 made CLS-06 the reclassification rule.
findings.evidence: engine_noshow.py:1100-1102: 'if tr.reclassified_to: return {"tier": f"n/a (reclassified to {tr.reclassified_to})", ... "gates": [] ...'. /tmp/a4check1/reclass_safety.py: 'rider_cancelled -> outcome None, reclass CW-RIDERCANCEL, tier n/a (reclassified to CW-RIDERCANCEL), gates [], safety True'. engine_gates.py: 'a tier the engine did not set (for example a reclassified case) counts as the lowest'.

findings.claim: fc_r01 (FC-F01's pricing mode in the engine) still reads only the trip flag. A trip whose accepted change is recorded as an app event (destination_edit_accepted or stop_added), which run() now treats as a change, therefore counts as FIXED_AT_BOOKING. FC-R01's 'no fare refund' (FC-R-FIXED-FARE) is applied to a fare that FC-F01, as changed in A4, calls RECALCULATED (FC-R03's domain).
findings.evidence: engine_toll.py:236: 'recalculated = _flag(trip.get("destination_edit_accepted"), False) is True                       # FC-F01: RECALCULATED'. FC-F01: 'becoming RECALCULATED if a destination edit (a changed drop-off or an added drop-off stop) was accepted.' /tmp/a4check1/toll2.py: 'F1 fc_r01, app event destination_edit_accepted only, base==quoted -> applies True, fare_refund 0.0, reason FC-R-FIXED-FARE'; 'F3 fc_r01 stop_added, no extra gantry -> applies True, fare_refund 0.0, reason FC-R-FIXED-FARE, toll_claim None'.
findings.failure_scenario: A RydeX route ticket with app_events=[stop_added] and quoted_fare equal to base_fare (the re-quoted fare). fc_r01 closes the fare part with FC-R-FIXED-FARE and a refund of 0. Under FC-F01 the fare is RECALCULATED, so FC-R03 (the detour measurement) should decide it.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the change once (the same test as run()'s 'changed') and use it in fc_r01 for RECALCULATED. Add a selftest case with a stop_added event.

findings.claim: CLS-06 has three gaps. (a) 'decide no fee until it arrives' can be read as 'decide that no fee is due' (a waiver); the zh says make no ruling on the fee. (b) REQUEST_INFO is labeled 'Ask the claimant for missing information', but the trip record is held by the platform, not the claimant. (c) A driver cancellation with a reason other than rider_no_show, with the fee charged, fits neither branch, because the records agree and say who canceled.
findings.evidence: CLS-06: 'the driver canceled with reason rider_no_show, CW-NOSHOW; the rider canceled, CW-RIDERCANCEL. If these records disagree, or none says who canceled, ... ask for the trip record (outcome REQUEST_INFO, reason GEN-R-NEED-INFO) and decide no fee until it arrives.' zh: '记录到之前不对收费作裁决'. taxonomy: '{code: REQUEST_INFO, label: Ask the claimant for missing information}'; '{code: GEN-R-NEED-INFO, label: Trip or charge cannot be identified, outcome: REQUEST_INFO}'. cls06.py: 'C7 reason driver_cancelled (no reason) + fee -> reclass CW-OTHER'.
findings.failure_scenario: An LLM applier given a silent record may output WAIVE_FEE ('no fee'), or may ask the rider for a record the rider cannot have. For a record of 'driver canceled, reason vehicle_issue, S$5 charged', CLS-06 sets no type and asks for nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Write 'make no ruling on the fee until the record arrives'. Say who is asked (the platform's trip record, and the claimant only for their own evidence). Add a branch: driver canceled with another reason and a fee charged gives CW-OTHER, escalated under GEN-R07.

findings.claim: Two smaller gaps in the classification rules. CLS-01's SE-type mapping and its safety examples leave out two TRIAGE_TO_HUMAN leaves (SE-MISMATCH, a driver or car that does not match the app, and SE-RECORDING). An applier that tests CLS-01 first may not create an SE claim for 'the car and driver did not match the app' when the ticket is about a fee. CLS-02 still says the organizer code stays primary when the text contradicts it, next to 'a safety claim ... is always the primary claim', without saying which wins.
findings.evidence: CLS-01: 'The SE type follows the taxonomy definitions (SE-CONDUCT for behavior toward a person, SE-DRIVING, SE-ACCIDENT, SE-TERMINATED for a ride ended midway, SE-OTHER otherwise).' CLS-02: 'A safety claim (any SE type ...) is always the primary claim; ... If the free text contradicts the organizer's dispute code, the code stays primary, the text's issue becomes a secondary claim'.
findings.failure_scenario: T13: 'I canceled because the car that came was a different model from the app and the driver looked different, and I was charged S$6.61.' This is not in CLS-01's list, so the applier may type it only as CW-RIDERCANCEL, eligible for an automatic ruling, instead of SE-MISMATCH primary at HUMAN. In a safety ticket filed under no_show_charge, the two CLS-02 sentences conflict about which claim is primary. That is outcome-neutral, because CLS-01 still routes the ticket to a person.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'a driver or vehicle that does not match the app' and 'a recording device in the car' to CLS-01's examples and its SE-type list. In CLS-02, write 'except that a safety claim is always primary'.

findings.claim: CW-R08's new definition of the advance-booking ETA (the scheduled time) leaves two waiver triggers for advance bookings that fire in the rider's favor. The 'not moving toward the pick-up point' ground is not qualified for an early driver who is parked and waiting. For an advance booking accepted after the cutoff, using the scheduled time instead of the app's assignment ETA makes a driver who is on time by the app 'late'.
findings.evidence: CW-R08: 'If, when the rider canceled, the driver was already later than the assignment ETA plus DRIVER_LATE_GRACE_S, or was not moving toward the pick-up point, the rider's cancellation fee is eligible for a waiver. ... For an advance booking the assignment ETA is the scheduled time (FairRyde's reading: the driver is due at the pick-up then).' CW-R02: 'if the request was accepted after that cut-off, the rider has a 3-minute grace period.'
findings.failure_scenario: An advance booking for 18:00, with the driver parked 300 m away at 17:50 waiting. The rider cancels at 17:50, which is chargeable under CW-R02. The driver is literally 'not moving toward the pick-up point', so the fee is waived. Or the booking is accepted at 17:55 with an app ETA of 10 minutes, the rider cancels at 18:04, and the driver is 'late' against the scheduled time, so the fee is waived. Both errors favor the rider, and CW-R08 is D, so the waiver needs approval.
findings.suggested_fix: For advance bookings, apply the 'not moving' ground only after the time the driver must leave to arrive by the scheduled time. Use the later of the scheduled time and the app's assignment ETA when the booking was accepted after the cutoff.

verdicts.reason: Read rules.yaml CLS-06 (lines 285-297: canceling party from cancellation_reason, the driver_cancelled or rider_cancelled event and the system message; records that disagree or say nothing give REQUEST_INFO) and the DT-CW-NOSHOW precondition (only 'reason rider_no_show, and no system message says the rider canceled'; A4 only added the CLS-06 citation). engine_noshow.py:410-416 is unchanged by A4 (step label still 'CLS-02, CW-R03') and reads only the reason and one regex. Reran /tmp/a4check1/cls06.py: C2 (reason rider_no_show plus a rider_cancelled app event) and C6 give UPHOLD R8 at AUTO, where CLS-06 requires REQUEST_INFO. C3 ('Rider cancelled the trip.') and C3c also give UPHOLD AUTO. C1 (silent record) and C8 give a CW-OTHER reclassification, not REQUEST_INFO. rider_cancelled events do occur in round 1 data (E05, E06), so the shape is realistic, though records that contradict each other are rare. The KB now holds two conflicting texts, and the reference engine follows the narrower one. The regex gap for C3 predates A4, so MAJOR rather than CRITICAL.

engine_toll.py:189-190 (new in A4) counts a change only when _flag(destination_edit_accepted) is exactly True, or when an event is named exactly destination_edit_accepted or stop_added. _flag returns None for unparseable text, and None is treated as 'not changed'. The same engine treats an unparseable is_carpool as FC-R12 (T39), and _active treats unparseable as the safe direction. Reran /tmp/a4check1/toll2.py: U1 with a timestamp, 'accepted' or 'edited' in the flag and a stale route equal to the actual gantries gives UPHOLD 0.00 AUTO; U2 (is_carpool 'maybe') gives HUMAN. toll.py E5 (destination_edit_fee line only), E6 (system chat only) and E9b ('destination_changed') also miss the change. A2 check round 2 rated the same class of finding (A2R2-03, literal booleans) MAJOR. Uncommon data shape in an in-scope type, so MAJOR is consistent.

Reran toll.py E8, E8b and E9. The outputs are exactly what the engine gives for a single-drop-off trip with the same route_review. The failure needs a recommended route on record that skips a booked stop, which is a wrong record; the engine trusts the route on record in every case, and A4 did not create that exposure. The KB text covers the case: FC-F02 defines the recommended route as 'from the pick-up through every drop-off in order', FC-R12 escalates when the recommended route is missing, and PB-FC-ROUTE's required evidence is 'precomputed recommended route through the final itinerary'. Asking for the final_itinerary marker only when the itinerary changed is principled, because only then is the route computed at booking known to be stale. At most, FC-R12 could name 'a booked stop the route on record skips' explicitly (a wording point).

Read FC-F02 (rules.yaml 1064-1080). Piece 1 'runs toward the drop-offs then in force' up to a moment in time, and piece 2 starts 'from where the car was'. When the car is off the recommended route at the change, the text does not say where piece 1's baseline ends or how its distance is measured. An applier can take the shortest path from P to X (6 km, so DR 1.0) and absorb a detour driven before the change. FC-F01 makes a fare RECALCULATED only after an accepted edit, and FC-R03 applies only to RECALCULATED fares, so every FC-R03 fare-refund case goes through this text, and a detour followed by a change is a plausible pattern in an in-scope type. The second point, that the stop sentence read literally excuses a detour on the leg to an added stop, is weak: the sentence follows by 'therefore' from measuring against the route through the stop. MAJOR rests on the undefined piece-1 baseline.

Reran /tmp/a4check1/safety_engine.py: 22 of 22 safety texts that use no listed word give UPHOLD AUTO, and V104 to V106 each hit a word A4 added ('told me to get out', 'let me out' and 'kidnap', 'racist'). The facts hold, but this is a documented limitation of a verification tool, not a KB error. CLS-01 is mode READ and its credibility note says SAFETY_WORDS is only an offline stand-in. The engine_noshow.py comment says the same, and D40(a) records it for Jasper (round 2's taxonomy texts test the definition). V104 to V106 are labeled accurately as 'without v0.1's words'. engine_toll's docstring limits it to the listed ERP rules (no CLS). rerun_engine.py's docstring calls itself 'a regression check, never a validation score', so the round 2 impact is overstated. The useful residue is a test-design point (add xfail meaning-only texts): MINOR.

Read the Code of Conduct in kb/sources/ryde_policy_corpus.json. Item 5's heading is 'Assault, harassment, or abuse of any kind will not be tolerated', and it adds 'drivers must not ask overly personal questions, comment on anyone's appearance, or contact passengers after a trip for personal reasons'. CLS-01 limits abuse to 'race, religion, nationality or disability', drops the community standards' 'etc', and leaves out the item 5 behaviors. That narrowing is real. But the line between rudeness and safety is explicitly labeled FairRyde design in CLS-01's FAIRRYDE note, so where to draw it is Jasper's call. Practical risk is limited for three reasons. SE-CONDUCT's new definition begins 'behavior ... that Ryde's Code of Conduct prohibits', which covers abuse of any kind by reference. CLS-01's examples are 'not a closed list', and unclear text counts as safety (S1). The rudeness carve-out names only 'a raised voice, scolding, an unfriendly manner', not insults or slurs. A text like T20 would most likely be read as S1.

Reran /tmp/a4check1/safety_engine.py. Routine texts give tier HUMAN through words A4 added: 'ok let me go down now' ('let me go'), 'left me stranded at the mall' ('stranded'), 'skyscraper' and 'therapeutic' ('rape' as a substring), 'stuck on the expressway' and 'speeding past the lobby'. This is the matching at engine_noshow.py:366 ('w in x.lower()'). These errors are in the safe direction (more HUMAN) and the corpus has no hits, so MINOR is right.

CLS-01 (rules.yaml 182-198) lists 'being left stranded at an isolated place or at night' and 'a driver or rider under the influence of drink or drugs' under 'being put in danger', and ties neither to a drop-off or to actual danger. A night-time cancellation-fee complaint or a drunk-rider vomit claim (the C20 pattern) can then be read as an SE claim. The direction is safe (HUMAN instead of AUTO or APPROVE; DM-CLEANING already needs approval). The intoxication trigger predates A4: v0.1's list had 'intoxication' and the engine had 'drunk'. Only 'stranded' is new. MINOR.

engine_noshow.py:1100-1102 returns tier 'n/a (reclassified ...)' with gates [] before the G4 check at 1155. Reran /tmp/a4check1/reclass_safety.py: rider_cancelled plus threat text gives safety True, no G4 and tier n/a. A4 did not change this code (the engine's diff touches only SAFETY_WORDS), and the reclassified result has no outcome, so no automatic ruling is made. engine_gates treats 'n/a' as the lowest tier only when G3 fires. Pre-existing and cosmetic for the engine: MINOR.

engine_toll.py:236 (fc_r01) still sets recalculated only from the trip flag, while A4's run() (189-190) also counts the destination_edit_accepted and stop_added events, and A4's FC-F01 says an accepted edit or added stop makes the fare RECALCULATED. Reran toll2.py: F1 (event only, base equal to quoted) and F3 (stop_added) give applies True and FC-R-FIXED-FARE. The trigger needs the record's quoted fare to equal the recalculated base fare (otherwise R3's path already stops FC-R01), and the engine does not implement FC-R03, so MINOR.

CLS-06's English 'decide no fee until it arrives' can be read as a waiver, while the zh says no ruling on the fee until the record arrives. Taxonomy line 599 labels REQUEST_INFO 'Ask the claimant for missing information', and line 652 labels GEN-R-NEED-INFO 'Trip or charge cannot be identified', but under CLS-06 the platform holds the record and the trip is identified. Both are wording mismatches. Point (c) is weak: a driver cancellation for another reason falls to CW-OTHER by its taxonomy definition ('Fits the category but no type above', BACKLOG, then GEN-R07), and the engine reclassifies it there (C7). MINOR overall.

CLS-01's SE-type parenthetical names SE-CONDUCT, SE-DRIVING, SE-ACCIDENT and SE-TERMINATED, then 'SE-OTHER otherwise', omitting the TRIAGE_TO_HUMAN leaves SE-MISMATCH and SE-RECORDING (taxonomy.yaml 315, 329). The examples do not mention a driver or vehicle that does not match the app. CLS-02 still has both 'A safety claim (any SE type) is always the primary claim' and 'If the free text contradicts the organizer's dispute code, the code stays primary'; the second sentence predates A4. Both lead to a person either way, so MINOR.

Read CW-R08 (rules.yaml 944-966) and CW-R02 (800-814). With A4's sentence (advance-booking ETA is the scheduled time) and DRIVER_LATE_GRACE_S of 180 s, a booking accepted at 17:55 for 18:00 (app ETA 10 min) makes the driver 'late' at 18:04 although the app's ETA has not passed. CW-R02 gives such late-accepted bookings only a 3-minute grace, so the fee would otherwise be chargeable. The 'not moving toward the pick-up point' ground for a parked, early driver predates A4, but A4 left it unqualified while defining CW-R08 for advance bookings. CW-R08 is D and the waiver needs approval: MINOR.

findings.claim: The new CLS-06 and the DT-CW-NOSHOW precondition (which A4 rewrote to cite CLS-06) give different outcomes when the cancellation records disagree or are silent, and the reference engine follows neither consistently: conflicting records yield an UPHOLD where CLS-06 requires REQUEST_INFO.
findings.evidence: CLS-06 (rules.yaml 291-295): 'classified by who canceled according to the trip record (trip_data.cancellation_reason, the driver_cancelled or rider_cancelled event, the system message) ... If these records disagree, or none says who canceled, the type cannot be set: ask for the trip record (outcome REQUEST_INFO, reason GEN-R-NEED-INFO)'. DT-CW-NOSHOW precondition (1988-1990): 'The trip record shows a cancellation with reason rider_no_show, and no system message says the rider canceled. Otherwise the claim is reclassified by who canceled (CLS-06: usually CW-RIDERCANCEL)'. engine_noshow.py 410-415: by_rider looks only at system chat; 'drv_cancel = t.get("cancellation_reason") == "rider_no_show" and not by_rider'; step labeled 'CLS-02, CW-R03'. Scratch run (/tmp/a4check1/cls06.py) on DISP-002: + app event rider_cancelled -> 'UPHOLD R8 [CW-R-NOSHOW-VALID, ...] tier APPROVE', rider told 'Outcome: the S$5.00 cancellation fee stands.'; system message changed to 'Trip cancelled by rider' (reason still rider_no_show) -> reclassified CW-OTHER; cancellation_reason removed -> reclassified CW-OTHER (not REQUEST_INFO).
findings.failure_scenario: A CW-NOSHOW ticket whose trip_data says rider_no_show while the app events record rider_cancelled: CLS-06 says the records disagree, so REQUEST_INFO and no fee decision; the DT precondition is met literally, so the table rules (R8 UPHOLD); the engine upholds the fee at APPROVE and tells the rider the fee stands. A ticket with no cancellation_reason: CLS-06 says REQUEST_INFO; the DT says reclassify (usually CW-RIDERCANCEL); the engine says CW-OTHER (backlog, GEN-R07 escalation).
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the DT-CW-NOSHOW precondition as 'CLS-06 types the claim CW-NOSHOW (driver canceled with reason rider_no_show and no record says otherwise); if the records disagree or none says who canceled, REQUEST_INFO and the table is not used'. Implement the same in engine_noshow.py step 1 (reason, cancelled_by, driver_cancelled/rider_cancelled events, system message), relabel the step 'CLS-06, CW-R03', and add self-tests for an event that disagrees, a system message that disagrees and a missing reason.

findings.claim: The engine and the explanation tell both parties that a recorded rider cancellation is 'handled under CW-OTHER' (a backlog type escalated by GEN-R07), while CLS-06 types it CW-RIDERCANCEL (an adjudicated type); round 1 cases E05 and E06 show it.

The party-facing sentence is false under the new rule. Outcome-neutral in the noshow engine itself (no ruling for reclassified cases).

I wait at the porch.' or 'Please follow messages, I'm at the porch' -> HUMAN, gate G4. verdicts.reason: Reproduced in /tmp/a4check1/sk_cons/cls06_sk.py. On cleaned DISP-002 with an app event rider_cancelled added (reason still rider_no_show, no system message about the rider), the engine returns UPHOLD R8 at tier AUTO. With the system message changed to 'Trip cancelled by rider' it reclassifies to CW-OTHER, and with cancellation_reason removed it also reclassifies to CW-OTHER. CLS-06 (rules.yaml 285-302) asks for REQUEST_INFO when the records disagree. engine_noshow.py 410-415 (step 1, labeled 'CLS-02, CW-R03') looks only at the system chat and the reason field, and A4 did not touch it: the only engine_noshow.py hunk in the diff is SAFETY_WORDS. So the reference engine does not implement CLS-06. I lowered the severity from CRITICAL for two reasons. (1) The KB itself is reconcilable. PB-INTAKE step 3 now runs CLS-06 before PB-CW-NOSHOW, so an applier following the playbooks reaches REQUEST_INFO at intake. The DT precondition and PB-CW-NOSHOW step 1 are narrower: they do not mention records that disagree. But both defer to CLS-06, so they do not contradict it. (2) The outcome-changing divergence needs trip records that contradict each other. That is a rare data-error pattern: no DISP-002 variant, E case or self-test has it, and the workflow's own rubric rates a rare unsafe error MAJOR. One correction to the finding: when only the reason is removed, DISP-002's system message still says 'cancelled by driver. Reason: rider_no_show', so CLS-06 would type the claim CW-NOSHOW, not REQUEST_INFO. The engine's CW-OTHER is wrong either way.

Ran /tmp/a4check1/sk_cons/e05.py on validation/V4_e2e/cases/E05.json and E06.json. Both have cancelled_by 'rider', reason 'rider_cancelled_eta_too_long' or 'rider_cancelled_change_of_plans', an app event rider_cancelled and the system message 'Trip cancelled by rider'. The engine sets reclassified_to CW-OTHER with tier 'n/a (reclassified to CW-OTHER)'. explain.noshow tells both parties: 'This claim is not a driver no-show cancellation, so it is handled under CW-OTHER.' The cause is engine_noshow.py 415, which checks for the exact string 'rider_cancelled'. CLS-06 types these claims CW-RIDERCANCEL, an adjudicated type in scope.yaml line 68, while CW-OTHER is BACKLOG. Outcome-neutral in the repo: the only consumers of reclassified_to are the n/a tier, the explanation and the selftest/build bookkeeping, and the noshow engine makes no ruling for reclassified cases. So it is wrong but outcome-neutral, which is MAJOR. The logic is older than A4, but it now contradicts the new CLS-06.

Reproduced in /tmp/a4check1/sk_cons/fp_sk.py with the real E01, E03 and E04 cases. E04 (WAIVE_FEE AUTO) plus the rider message 'ok let me go down now' gives WAIVE_FEE HUMAN with gate G4. The driver messages "I'm waiting at the side, the grape stall" ('rape'), 'Stuck on the expressway, 2 min.', 'Please follow messages...' ('follow me' matches inside 'follow messages') and 'Cannot stop at the main road, dangerous...' all move E01 and E03 from APPROVE to HUMAN and E04 from AUTO to HUMAN. In every run both parties get the safety notice. The cause is the plain substring match at engine_noshow.py 366 over A4's new entries. I kept MAJOR rather than CRITICAL. The direction is safe, and CLS-01 itself sends unclear text to a person. The authoritative rule is the READ definition, and D40 (a) records the stand-in as erring toward safety. None of the 1,337 existing corpus and E-case texts (cw_f06_reading_corpus.json plus V4 cases) triggers any new word (corpus_sk.py), so these are not frequent in current data. D40 (a) does not record substring false positives such as 'grape' or 'follow messages', so the defect stands.

explain.py 81-84 is as quoted. With E04 plus the driver message 'Rider shouted and threatened me when I called.', the rider is told 'Your report includes a safety concern' and the driver 'The rider's report includes a safety concern' (fp_sk.py). The same happens for every driver-side trigger above. The text is wrong about who raised the concern. But explain.py is not in the A4 diff, and pre-A4 CLS-01 already scanned all free text including chat, so this is older than A4. The tier and outcome are unaffected, and the fix is a neutral rewording. That makes it a wording defect (MINOR), not MAJOR.

Reproduced in /tmp/a4check1/sk_cons/fcr01_sk.py. _erp_case(CTE+PIE, recommended [CTE]) with only an app event destination_edit_accepted, or only stop_added, gives fc_r01 applies True, fare_refund 0.0, FC-R-FIXED-FARE. It is a rare pattern in a reference helper that only the self-test uses, and the toll part still escalates. So MAJOR, not CRITICAL.
